headline: Front End Developer
summary: Front end developer: four years at JPMorgan Chase, leading a React and TypeScript interface, helping launch a customer-facing account-opening application and building a drag-and-drop page builder for the bank's UI component library. Designs and builds accessible products alone, checked against WCAG 2.2 AA end to end.

text.services: Owned three of its services until handoff, among them the Kafka-to-SSE adapter that streams application status and eligibility to the browser in real time and an aggregator that gives the interface all it needs in one response.
text.lead: Served six months as interim lead for eight engineers (code review, mentoring, sprint ceremonies, roadmap planning with product) and shipped the MVP of a deceased-notification tool for customers and beneficiaries.

text.interface: Led the design, testing and release of a React/TypeScript interface with Redux; built Java Spring Boot microservices and integrated enterprise APIs.

projects.name: 0VERTRAINED
projects.stack: React, Vite, PWA, Web Push, Netlify Functions, Supabase
bullets: React PWA for athletes who lift and race, designed and built alone: its own design system, broadsheet layouts on wide screens, a workout session runner, web push and lazy-loaded tab bundles.
In beta on version 19.6 with 2,030 automated tests; a seeded demo mode drives the same screens with fixed data.

projects.name: Caduceus
bullets: Review interface for a prior-authorization agent, designed for office staff who are not technical: plain language, a text-size control, and every screen checked against WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core, down to 320 px wide.
Shows its work: a "What was sent to the model" view puts the de-identified text in front of the reviewer.

projects.name: Portfolio
projects.stack: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, WebGL 2, no framework
bullets: A WebGL 2 view of the Santa Fe sky computed from the real positions of the sun, moon and stars, with a CSS fallback, reduced-motion and color-scheme support, and no build step.

projects.name: Lattice
bullets: Operator interface and guided public tour for a robot-fleet control plane: mission state, approvals for detours and handoffs, and replays of recorded runs.
